card.title: Could You Just…
card.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.

mechanism: A turns holding bouquet stems into successive wiring and finishing favors that transfer most of assembly to B.
confusable: Unlike accepting one suggestion, A must make each fix the basis of another small request.
comparison: D25-b uses a snag warning to recruit the finishing work; D25-a uses aligned screws to recruit the rest of installation.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
